Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> International | National Over 6,000 visas revoked in crackdown on foreigners seeking US-born babies’ citizenship Source : Myjoyonline 16 November 2026 9:49am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The United States has revoked more than 6,000 visas and intensified efforts to dismantle international networks suspected of facilitating birth tourism and visa fraud.
The US Department of State says investigations have uncovered suspected operations in West Africa, Europe and North Africa, involving fraudulent documents and individuals who help foreign nationals obtain visitor visas to travel to the country primarily to give birth.
In West Africa, a US embassy uncovered a suspected network involving more than 100 foreign nationals who allegedly used fraudulent documents and visa facilitators, commonly known as fixers, to arrange childbirth-related travel.
The department said the operation had been shut down, with the visas of those involved revoked, although it did not identify the country where the network was discovered.
In Europe, investigators identified more than 400 suspected cases dating back to 2024, reportedly linked to at least six companies accused of coaching visa applicants, arranging accommodation and organising childbirth plans in the United States.
Another investigation in North Africa resulted in the revocation of more than 100 visas belonging to parents suspected of travelling to the US primarily to secure citizenship for their children.
The investigations form part of a wider crackdown by President Donald Trump's administration on commercial birth tourism.
On August 12, 2026, the State Department established a Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force to investigate suspected cases, revoke visas and dismantle networks facilitating the practice. The department subsequently announced that the task force had revoked more than 6,000 visas worldwide.
On September 23, Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced additional visa restrictions targeting individuals who knowingly facilitate commercial birth tourism, including operators of such networks and visa intermediaries.
The measures were introduced under Section 212(a)(3)(C) of the Immigration and Nationality Act.
Under US visa regulations introduced in January 2020, visitor visas cannot be issued to applicants whose primary purpose for travelling is to give birth in the country to obtain American citizenship for their children.
However, the restriction does not automatically prevent pregnant women from travelling to the US. Those seeking legitimate medical treatment may still qualify for visitor visas if they meet the relevant requirements, including demonstrating the purpose of treatment and their ability to cover the costs.
The visa restrictions are also separate from the constitutional principle of birthright citizenship.
On June 30, 2026, the US Supreme Court reaffirmed in Trump v. Barbara that children born in the United States to parents who are temporarily or unlawfully present are citizens at birth under the Fourteenth Amendment.
The current enforcement measures therefore target alleged visa abuse and the commercial networks facilitating birth tourism rather than automatically removing citizenship rights from children born in the country.
